title: Childproof a two-door cabinet with a U-shaped slide lock across its knobs
instruction: Childproof this cabinet: fit the slide lock across the two door knobs so that the doors cannot be opened, then take your hands away.
context: Parents of crawling toddlers lock every low cabinet within reach. For two doors with knobs, the standard fix is a U-shaped slide lock: the U's two rods go behind both knob heads, one above and one below the knob stems, and a lock block slides onto the rod ends until it is snug against the far knob. The U has to be held in place behind the knobs while the block's two holes are lined up with the two rod ends. Many first-time parents find this fiddly. Cabinets with cleaning products and medicines are the reason: every day more than 300 children in the US are treated in an emergency department for poisoning (CDC).
setup: Two arms on the floor in front of a low cabinet (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them; heights are above the floor. (1) A low two-door cabinet such as a TV console, 63 cm wide and 40 cm deep, white, standing on the floor with its door fronts 37 cm forward, centred on the centre line. Its top board is 66 cm wide and 2 cm thick, 28 to 30 cm above the floor, and overhangs the doors by 2.2 cm. Two 19 mm MDF doors, 29.4 cm wide and 26.6 cm tall (bottoms 4 mm above the floor), meet on the centre line with a 3 mm gap. They are hung at their outer edges on self-closing hinges and open outwards, towards the arms. (2) On each door a brushed-nickel round knob: a 32 mm head, 15 mm thick, on a 12 mm stem standing 25 mm off the door (4 cm projection). The knobs are centred 4.5 cm left and right of the centre line, 20 cm above the floor. (3) A white plastic U-shaped cabinet slide lock (Safety 1st Cabinet Slide Lock 11002 type), in two parts lying flat on the floor. The U: two 6 mm round rods 17 cm long with tapered ends, 2.1 cm clear between them, joined at one end by a flat grip 4.0 x 1.2 x 1.0 cm; 30 g. Its grip lies 20 cm forward and 15 cm left of the centre line, with the rods pointing right. The lock block: 5.7 x 2.0 x 1.7 cm, 25 g, with two 9 mm square holes 2.7 cm apart running through its 2 cm length, chamfered on one face. It lies 20 cm forward and 15 cm right of the centre line, with its holes running left-right and the chamfered face to the left. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: 1.0 as soon as all of these hold, with the U and the block still, for 1 s: the U's rods behind both knob heads, one rod above and one below both knob stems; the lock block on both rod ends (at least 5 mm of each rod inside it); the lock snug: from the U grip's inner face to the block's inner face at most 11.2 cm (the knob stems' outer span plus 1 cm, so the doors can be pulled at most about 1 cm apart); both doors shut (within 3 degrees); and each gripper's fingertip centre at least 6 cm in front of the door fronts (2 cm in front of the knob heads). Otherwise, judged at the end of the run: 0.75: the same, but a gripper closer to the doors; 0.5: the U round both stems and the block on both rods, but not snug or a door open; 0.25: the U round both stems but the block not on both rods; 0.0: anything else. In a real trial each part is checked by eye and the 11.2 cm with a ruler.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Press the block's release button and slide it off the rods, take the U out from behind the knobs, shut both doors, and lay the U and the block on the floor as in the screenshot.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1 with PhysX, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm rig. Simplified: the cabinet is modelled only at its front, the doors hang on spring hinges against the face frame, the lock's ratchet teeth and release button are not modelled (the block slides on the rods against friction only), all parts are built from boxes and cylinders, and the cameras render at 320 x 176.
